newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST - US vote, then productivity data 11/4 wk.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - US vote, then productivity data 11/4 wk.

text.p: The U.S. Presidential elections and the Treasury's quarterly refunding are expected to overshadow a light economic calendar next week.
However, among a series of second-tier indicators, productivity should garner the most attention, experts said in a Reuters poll.

"I don't think the numbers coming out next week are big market movers or shakers," said Cheryl Katz, senior economist at Merrill Lynch and Co. But the central bank may keep an eye on productivity and labor costs, she said.
The Labor Department is set to release third-quarter preliminary productivity and labor costs on Thursday, November 7 at 1000 EST/1500 GMT.
On average, experts forecast productivity to have declined 0.1 percent in the third quarter from an increase of 0.5 percent in the prior quarter.
Respondents forecast, on average, labor costs to have risen 3.7 percent in the third quarter. The second-quarter figure was pegged at 3.2 percent.
